SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-07: FHIRPath — §5.5.4 Date Conversion, §5.5.5 DateTime Conversion, §5.5.6 Decimal Conversion. Test these items: toDate(), convertsToDate(), toDateTime(), convertsToDateTime(), toDecimal(), convertsToDecimal(). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath N1 §5.5.1 (DateTime representation; Z for UTC) + dual-engine lockstep invariant
issues.evidence: Python fallback FP_DateTime._extractDateByPrecision (engine/nodes.py) normalized an authored 'Z' timezone to '+00:00' when rendering temporal ARITHMETIC results: '@2020-06-30T23:59:59Z + 1 second' -> fallback '2020-07-01T00:00:00+00:00' vs native '2020-07-01T00:00:00Z'. Also affected .toDateTime()-converted operands, '- 1 second', '+ 1 minute', millisecond-precision results, and '+ 0 seconds' identity. Authored '+hh:mm' offsets and plain conversion/equality were already correct in both engines. No official fixture pins Z-suffixed arithmetic output, so engine parity governs.
issues.root_cause: Explicit '# Normalize Z to +00:00 for consistent output' branch in FP_DateTime._extractDateByPrecision diverged from the native evaluator's preserve-authored-spelling behavior
issues.resolution: Removed the Z->+00:00 normalization; timezone_str is appended verbatim, preserving authored 'Z' spelling. Python-only fix (no extension rebuild). Regression: test_temporal_arithmetic_preserves_authored_z_suffix_parity_fp07_explorer in test_conversion_parity.py (11 cases, native vs forced fallback).
issues.verified_in: test_conversion_parity.py 41/41; full conformance 2832/2832 (ViewDef 144, FHIRPath 935, CQL 1706, DQM 47)
